findings.rule: Title block heat treatment field must not be blank or '---' when a heat treatment note is specified on the drawing.
findings.reasoning: The title block heat_treatment field is '---', but note N1 specifies case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a 0.8–2 mm case depth. A manufacturer reading only the title block would skip heat treatment entirely, producing a soft part that fails in service.
findings.correction: Update the title block heat_treatment field to reference N1 (e.g., 'CASE HARDEN PER NOTE N1') or explicitly state 'CASE HARDENED 55-60 HRC'.

findings.rule: Hole depth-to-diameter ratio should generally not exceed 10:1 for standard drilling without specialized deep-hole processes.
findings.reasoning: Feature F4 calls for a Ø4.2 mm hole (D14) drilled 50 mm deep (D15), giving a depth-to-diameter ratio of nearly 12:1. This exceeds standard twist-drill capability, risks drill breakage and wander, and requires costly gun-drilling or peck-drilling with special tooling.
findings.correction: Redesign the part to shorten the hole depth if functionally possible, or explicitly specify a deep-hole drilling process (e.g., gun drill) and add an appropriate tolerance/straightness callout.

findings.rule: Functional diameters such as bearing seats, pin fits, or sleeve ODs/IDs require explicit tolerances or fit classes to ensure assembly and function.
findings.reasoning: The outer diameter (Ø30, D1/D13) and inner bore (Ø20, D4/D12) have no tolerances specified. As a 'TCP PIN SLEEVE', these are functional mating surfaces; falling back on the general machining tolerance of ±0.5 mm (for the 6–30 mm range) or ±0.8 mm (for the 30–120 mm range) is far too loose for a sleeve fit and will result in improper assembly or excessive play.
findings.correction: Add appropriate fit-class tolerances (e.g., h7/H7) or specific dimensional tolerances to the functional outer and inner diameters.
